exclusions.reason: Letterhead, author credentials, thanks and prior internal 2023 proposal provenance are incidental. Future staffing demand is explicitly “vermutlich”; attractiveness, family friendliness and maintaining high standards are policy aims, not established causal outcomes. 2019 timing and demographic premise separately assessed.

Approval of catalogue pruning, placement of governance content and whether restructuring concepts should be tested are normative expert choices. “Typically” experience and going-concern relevance are retained as factual premises. Typical future use of the eight-year maximum is a forecast.

Proposed detailed two-tax-paper topic allocation, better breadth, less deterrence and automatic quality maintenance are recommendations/predictions. Whole-wage-tax example is a hypothetical illustration; existing absence of statutory numerical weights and comparator exam structure assessed separately.

Whether skills need to be tested four times, one obligatory oral is optimal and three attempts strike an appropriate public/private balance are normative. Actual burden and questioning-practice assertions assessed rather than excluded. Integration of nonfinancial topics is a proposal.

Judgements that one four-hour sustainability paper suffices, future planning certainty, bureaucracy is unnecessary/disproportionate, and broader exemptions are desirable are normative or unmeasured forecasts. Underlying legal timings, safeguards and methodology premise assessed. Repeated conclusion does not add claims.

Open-book permission, publishing model answers, more professional committee representatives and transparency are recommendations. Better applied competence is a forecast. Routine use of pronouncements retained for factual assessment; signatures/contact material incidental.

Authored date and joint authorship logged; addresses, general member self-description, thanks and favourable overall assessment are incidental or evaluative. No delivery inference from later ZIP filename date.

Proposals for more permeable admission/credit and future recruitment benefit are preferences/forecasts. Current statutory scope, legal need for future legislation and relevant competence overlap assessed; no assertion of already-proven course equivalence is attributed.
Whether vocational demand level deserves equal policy attention and should determine reform is normative. All specific current-law, qualification content/stage and DQR premises are retained.
Calls to use EU discretion and amend WPO are normative. Actual EU options, limits and distinct audit-practice requirements are retained; no claim of direct individual entitlement manufactured.

Proposed future section 13b amendment and conditional equivalence-testing criteria are recommendations. The text expressly leaves whether/how much concrete equivalence exists for later assessment; no claim of automatic equivalence is invented.

Expected career perspectives, recruitment potential and improved permeability are forecasts or policy aims; offers of dialogue and contact details are incidental. Competence-domain premise merged with pages 2–3.

limits: Full original first pass completed before previous targeted dispositions or counterpart inventory review.
Selected sections of long supporting laws/statistics only; no new long screening targets.
All claims conservatively assessed as of the printed response dates. No error is inferred from unavailable exact September bytes, unsupported expert inference or inaccessible empirical records.
No author contact or human specialist confirmation. Future demand, take-up, optimum design and speculative competence outcomes are not treated as observed outcomes.
Primary supporting downloads temporary; local evidence artifact is explicitly an authored concise check note, with original URL/access time/hash and read extent.
